PullRequest.Title: ci: run the browser unit tests in WebKit on Linux in the merge queue
PullRequest.Body:
Runs the browser unit tests in WebKit on Linux in the merge queue, as a required check, to catch WebKit regressions before they reach the product build.

**Why:** from Oct 19 to Nov 18, 8 code changes broke main CI (pipeline 727) only on macOS, keeping main red for about 45 h in total. **7 of the 8 were browser unit tests that failed only in WebKit**, which PR CI and the merge queue never run (they run Chromium). Main CI and the product build run WebKit on macOS, after merge. In each case the culprit added or changed the failing test in its own diff, so the test plan selected it, but nothing ran it in WebKit before merge. Three of them also failed releasing insider builds, and one, #348704, cost a release.

**What changes**

- `pr-linux-test.yml` gets a `Linux / Browser-Unit (WebKit)` job on the shared steps (`UNIT_TEST_BROWSER: webkit`). It installs WebKit with its system packages and runs the unit test files the plan selects, with `--rerun-failed-files 2` as the other unit jobs do.
  - A failure fails PR Gate, so a WebKit regression can't merge. If it turns out noisy, we revert.
  - Its 12 min job timeout keeps it within the merge queue's slowest job (Windows WSL smoke, about 13 min), which PR Gate waits for anyway.
- `pr.yml` runs it only for `merge_group`, when the plan selects browser unit tests. `detectChanges.test.ts` covers the new check.
- 12 tests that fail reliably in WebKit on Linux skip themselves there, each with a comment giving the reason:
  - `chatListRenderer.test.ts`: the `generated image preview loading` suite (4 tests), where the embedded image doesn't decode. Also `coalesces working progress updates from a burst of tool activity (complete=false)`, where the burst can take two frames to coalesce, and which failed 3 attempts in a row.
  - `chatResourceGroupWidget.test.ts`: 4 tests. The image fixture doesn't decode.
  - `chatPills.test.ts`: the 2 automatic compact mode tests. The runner's fonts measure the labels wider, so one more pill collapses.
  - `chatWorkingLogoAtlas.test.ts`: 1 test. The atlas canvas reads back blank.

**Skipping a test in WebKit on Linux.** Playwright's Linux WebKit is a different port from WebKit on macOS (Safari's engine), and a few tests fail there for port reasons rather than VS Code bugs. Such a test skips itself, the same way tests skip on other platforms, and says why:

```ts
import { isLinuxWebKit } from '<...>/base/test/browser/linuxWebKit.js';

// WebKit on Linux (Playwright's port) can't decode the image fixture, unlike Chromium and WebKit on macOS
const testUnlessLinuxWebKit = isLinuxWebKit ? test.skip : test;
```

`isLinuxWebKit` is needed because Playwright's Linux WebKit reports Safari's **macOS** user agent, so `isLinux` is false there. It checks `isSafari` and `navigator.platform` instead. Note that mocha's `test.skip` returns nothing, so a test that chains `.timeout(...)` needs `?.timeout(...)`. These tests still run in Chromium on every PR, and in WebKit on macOS in pipeline 727 and the product build.

**Why per-test skips rather than a list.** An earlier version of this PR kept a central JSON list of known failures and inverted their results in the runner. Per-test skips are simpler and safer:
- The owner of a test sees the skip next to the code, and removes it when they fix the test, as with the other platform skips.
- No runner machinery. Inverting mocha's results from outside had subtle failure modes: suite-level hooks, tests that change their own timeout, and fake timers. Review found all of them.
- Skip only what fails every time. On the runner, 21 of the 32 tests on the old list passed in some runs, and several then failed again. Those are left to `--rerun-failed-files`.

**Validation**

- PR CI proof on current main (base `e500efaccc`), with a temporary commit (now dropped) that ran the job for pull requests: [run 44432611157](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44432611157) passed 3 times out of 3 (the job plus 2 reruns), with the whole suite selected, about 57,000 tests. The test step took 7 to 8 min. `--rerun-failed-files` absorbed 2, 2 and 0 timing flakes, each a different test that passed in the other attempts (two `ContextView` window tests, then two generated-image reveal tests), so none of them is skipped.
- An earlier proof on an older base, [run 44173326667](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44173326667), also passed 3 times out of 3.
- The job already caught a real regression. In [run 44170937958](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44170937958), before #348930 was included, it failed on #348704's new test, which calls `new Touch(...)`, illegal in desktop WebKit. Pipeline 727 (main CI) caught the same test on macOS after merge (498256), and in the merge queue this job would have stopped it.
- The skipped tests come from 4 runs of the whole suite on the runner: 11 of them failed in all 4 runs, plus the coalescing test above.
- At `cad887fdb1`, before the first regression was fixed, its test fails in WebKit on Linux (`Sessions - Floating Details`, 250/150 ms instead of 200/100). The second regression's cause, a WebKit error message that doesn't match `/circular/`, also reproduces on Linux.
- `build/lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts` passes. The one failing Detect Changes test, the distro-commit one, fails the same way on main on Windows.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: Merge queue runs selected browser unit tests in the new Linux WebKit job, including full-suite fallback.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detect Changes must finish before the reusable Linux workflow starts. The new job performs setup, installs WebKit, and runs tests sequentially within its runner. PR Gate waits for linux-tests as well as sibling workflows; this is an additional parallel gate dependency, not an unconditional serial stage before all other tests. The whole WebKit job has a 12-minute timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml: Download the workspace image scripts; Restore the workspace image; .github/workflows/workspace_image/image.ts:restoreImage/unpack
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download four setup files from GitHub, locate one workspace-image artifact, and download/decompress/write its nonempty chunks before mounting its filesystem.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional setup sequence per eligible merge group; image requests scale with compressed image chunks, bounded to 32 concurrent download workers, not with selected test count. Restoration is limited to 240 seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every previously enabled Linux test job already performed this preparation independently; there was no additional WebKit job performing it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish or fall back before checkout and dependency setup; contributes to this job's readiness and potentially gate completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml: Restore pnpm store cache; Restore built-in extensions cache; .github/actions/install-linux-packages/action.yml; build/lib/builtInExtensions.ts:getBuiltInExtensions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore dependency/package/extension caches, or download missing npm packages, apt packages, and platform-applicable built-in extensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One set of cache lookups per new job. Cold downloads scale with missing package graph and applicable extension definitions, not per unit test; warm pnpm and extension state avoid the corresponding downloads. Extension streams can run concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cache-aware setup already ran once in each existing test job; this PR adds one such job rather than changing cache keys or invalidation for existing jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Setup must complete before transpilation and tests; cold or failed caches increase setup duration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml: shared steps Install build dependencies, Install dependencies, Setup system services, Fontconfig diagnostics and cache reset, Transpile client and extensions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run pnpm installation, native-build environment setup, system-service/font-cache preparation, and esbuild transpilation on the additional runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared preparation sequence per eligible new job; each pnpm installation has at most five workflow-level attempts. Compilation scales with source/extension inputs and dependency setup with cache misses, independently of N.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing browser-unit jobs used the same preparation. No new WebKit runner existed, and none of the existing jobs' preparation was moved earlier or repeated more often.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sequential prerequisites for the WebKit test step; Electron setup and browser integration/smoke compilation are gated off for this unit-only job.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps webkit, crossing package-manager/network/filesystem boundaries for the WebKit binary and required system packages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One invocation on success, at most three workflow-level attempts separated by five-second sleeps. One WebKit installation serves the entire job and all workers; it is not performed per test file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no Linux WebKit job or installation on this merge-queue path. Chromium jobs continue using their existing browser image/cache and installation branch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the test plan download and before any WebKit tests; uncached downloads add setup cost on eligible merge-group jobs only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch W Node worker processes and W fresh, potentially multiprocess WebKit browsers; each worker uses one browser/context/page for its assigned test execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: W browser launches initially, not N; W is bounded by CPU, memory and selected-file count. Tests with attributable failures may add up to two sequential fresh-browser launches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The browser runner already used identical bounded workers, claims, and retry behavior for Chromium; this PR adds a separate execution in WebKit without altering the runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Test completion is necessary for this job and PR Gate. Workers execute concurrently while reruns are serial.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serve modules/CSS over local HTTP, claim test files through synchronous local requests backed by filesystem claims, and serialize Mocha progress/results across the Playwright boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Module imports can scale as W*N, with imports cached within each browser's module graph. Claims scale with attempted file claims across bounded W workers; actual test-file execution is distributed. Reporting scales with executed test/hook events. This is another browser run, not a changed reporting or claim algorithm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing Chromium browser tests already used this same initialization, synchronous claiming, serialization, and cleanup. The diff adds coverage in another engine, not an extra inner loop or missing cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Module initialization, claims, and result reporting occur on the test execution path. Server disposal and browser close are awaited after each attempt.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional runner per eligible merge-group run. N is the unique selected compiled browser test files after runList Set filtering and exclusion of Node/Electron-only folders; without a usable plan, N is all browser test files. Each of W workers imports all N files, but filesystem-backed claims distribute test-file execution rather than executing the whole suite W times.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A separate 8-core merge-queue runner executes the new job independently of Chromium and other jobs. W is capped at 4, available CPUs, and one worker per 2 GiB of total memory. With a run list, W is additionally min(fileCount, max(2, floor(fileCount/75))), with a minimum of 1. Image restoration uses at most 32 connections and a bounded 64-chunk decompression window. No new per-test browser launch or unbounded worker fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workspace images of main retain dependencies and the pnpm store; image restore failure falls back to cached-store/cold installation. Linux system packages have an image/version/list-keyed deb cache. Built-in extensions have a content-keyed cache and version checks. The Linux workspace image installs only Chromium, and this new job does not restore a WebKit browser cache, so successful fresh jobs download WebKit even when the workspace image is warm. Within an installation retry, completed files can be reused. Test selection remains artifact-driven and fails open to the whole suite.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the new gate dependency, uncached WebKit installation, cache-aware shared setup, bounded worker count, all-files-per-worker imports, and distributed test execution, established directly from workflow and runner code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured runner durations, cache-hit rates, queue contention, or selected-file distributions were independently available. The additional uncached installation and test run can increase gate latency when this job becomes the slowest sibling; the repository's timing comments are not treated as proof that it never does.
Scenarios.Verdict: Intentional additional engine coverage entails real bounded setup/test cost. No high-confidence accidental performance regression, defeated existing cache, per-file process fan-out, or new lifecycle leak was established. Reporting the mere addition of this required test job or suggesting a cache without a demonstrated regression would not meet the finding standard.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ordinary pull requests and merge groups with no selected browser unit tests.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing change detection and selected jobs determine PR Gate readiness. WebKit is disabled for all pull_request events and for successfully detected merge groups without browser tests, so its setup is off the path entirely.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml:378-403 Restore Playwright browsers / Install Playwright Chromium
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore or install the previously used Chromium headless-shell binary for existing browser jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged: cache restore when no workspace image was used, and one installation sequence per enabled existing browser job, at most three attempts on failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cache restore and Chromium installation steps ran under BROWSER_TESTS; the added non-webkit guard remains true for all existing job environments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Same prerequisite for existing browser tests; no new work for ordinary PRs or browser-unaffected merge groups.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Event type and selected-browser-unit-tests boolean; existing Chromium test selection retains the same effective unique-file cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing jobs retain their previous scheduling and browser worker limits. A skipped WebKit job allocates no runner and launches no test workers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing Chromium workspace-image/browser-cache behavior is preserved: undefined UNIT_TEST_BROWSER satisfies the non-webkit branch. No WebKit cache lookup or installation occurs when its job condition is false.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both the caller's merge_group guard and the reusable job's input guard were inspected, together with existing job environments and Chromium step conditions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing CI duration and cache-hit distributions are unmeasured, but they do not affect the established absence of additional WebKit work in these scenarios.
Scenarios.Verdict: No added expensive path or increased cardinality for ordinary PRs and browser-unaffected merge groups.

Scenarios.Scenario: Register and run the changed chat image, progress-coalescing, canvas-atlas and responsive-pill browser tests.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Test modules are imported and register suites before Mocha execution. The new platform helper evaluates a constant browser/platform predicate. Selected Linux WebKit tests are pending and their bodies/hooks do not run; other engines continue running the same bodies.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Four importing test files and a fixed set of platform-specific skips: four generated-image suite tests, four resource-group tests, one progress-coalescing case, one atlas test, and two responsive-pill tests. The helper is evaluated once per browser module graph, not per rendered chat row, frame or user interaction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Follows the already inspected bounded runner workers; the helper introduces no tasks, listeners, timers, browsers, or parallel work. Optional timeout chaining changes only skipped-test registration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ES module evaluation is cached within each browser realm. The helper stores one boolean and does not create a growing cache or retain resources. Test fixtures and product rendering code are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every changed test hunk and the complete helper were inspected, its browser import was traced, and repository references remain confined to tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measurements of skipped test duration are available; skipping bodies cannot establish a new rendering or I/O cost. Production chat runtime is not changed by these test-only imports.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. These changes remove selected test-body work only in Linux WebKit and do not alter product chat rendering, image allocation, progress coalescing, canvas generation or pill layout. They are not evidence of a shipped performance-regression fix.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed assertions synchronously read/parse workflow YAML and enumerate test jobs before asserting expected checks and predicates. No actual CI jobs are launched by these tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read workflow YAML files synchronously and parse their jobs for consistency assertions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same number of workflow-file reads per assertion before and after; one additional job definition is processed in the existing Linux YAML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same helpers read pr.yml and the same reusable workflow files; only expected job membership and the new predicate differ.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronous prerequisite within this small build-test scenario, not product startup or UI input.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing fixed set of reusable workflow files and job definitions; the new WebKit job adds one map entry and expected-array item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing Node test scheduling is unchanged. testJobs enumerates jobs synchronously and reads each referenced workflow once per invocation, not once for every job inside that workflow.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: loadWorkflow has no memoization, but the diff does not increase its invocation count or introduce a new reusable workflow file. YAML alias resolution continues sharing the common steps.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed assertions and loadWorkflow/testJobs implementations were traced directly; detector API calls are mocked and unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Parsing the larger YAML adds a small fixed amount of work; no realistic scaling amplification or latency problem is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable regression; fixed-size test expectation changes preserve boundary-call counts.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across the full eight-file inventory and every diff page against base 72ebe055d56345a7b8c8d611b786c7721f87eb7e. Traced merge-queue/PR gate scheduling, cache preparation, WebKit installation, worker and retry cardinality, local HTTP/IPC/filesystem boundaries, cleanup, and test-only imports/assertions. No qualifying introduced performance findings or concrete performance-regression fixes. Static review; timings and runner contention were not measured. Supporting focus documents were requested; the guide response was tool-truncated.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
